messages.content: I want to settle the Seattle flights now. Monday starts at 9:00 at the Sheraton, so keep the Sunday night stay. Can we compare the two Sunday departures and the Wednesday returns around the meetings?

Yes. Sunday, June 15 is the right travel day for the Monday opening. From the shortlist, the earlier Denver nonstop reaches Seattle with enough time to get downtown, check in, and attend the informal publisher dinner. The later nonstop is less expensive but arrives after the dinner begins. On Wednesday, June 18, your last meeting ends at 3:30 p.m.; the first viable return leaves shortly after 7:00, while the later nonstop gives you more breathing room from downtown.
How much usable time would I have before that Sunday dinner with the earlier flight?

Assuming the listed on-time arrival, allow roughly 30 minutes to get off the plane and collect your bag, then 35 to 60 minutes to reach the downtown hotel. That should leave about 60 to 90 minutes to check in and get to dinner. A significant delay would reduce that cushion, but the plan is workable.
And the later flight definitely misses it?

Yes. Even with an on-time arrival and a quick car ride, you would reach downtown after the planned dinner start. It only works if you are comfortable skipping the dinner and going directly to the hotel.
The dinner is useful because several press people will be there. The earlier fare was about $85 more, correct?

That was the difference in the options previously surfaced, before any bag, seat, or fare-rule differences. Since the dinner has professional value and the earlier arrival also protects against a tighter evening, the extra $85 is reasonable. The live total still needs to be checked before purchase.
All right, use the earlier Sunday nonstop. For Wednesday, could I realistically make the first return if I leave the meeting at 3:30?

It is possible but not especially forgiving. You would need to collect the roller from the hotel promptly and leave downtown around 4:00 to 4:15. Normal traffic should put you at SEA with adequate time, but a meeting overrun, slow bag retrieval, or heavy traffic could make the airport window uncomfortable.
I do not want to spend the last meeting watching the clock. How much later is the other nonstop?

The later option departs roughly an hour after the first one. That gives you time to finish at 3:30, handle a brief closing conversation, collect your bag, and head to SEA without needing every step to go perfectly. It gets you back to Denver later that night, but avoids adding another hotel night.
Choose the later Wednesday nonstop, then. Please give me the pair and the timing I should protect, without treating anything as ticketed yet.

Use the earlier nonstop from Denver to Seattle on Sunday, June 15, arriving early enough for hotel check-in and the publisher dinner. Keep the Sunday-night hotel stay. On Wednesday, June 18, take the later evening nonstop to Denver after the 3:30 p.m. meeting; collect your stored bag and aim to leave downtown by about 4:45, earlier if traffic is building. Before purchase, verify the live flight numbers and times, total fares, baggage and change terms, and the dinner start time. Nothing for Seattle has been booked yet.
